definition: John Joseph Hopfield (born July 15, 1933) is an American physicist and emeritus professor of Princeton University, most widely known for his study of associative neural networks in 1982.
details: Developed associative neural networks that use statistical physics principles to store and retrieve patterns. He is known for the development of the Hopfield network. Before its invention, research in artificial intelligence (AI) was in a decay period or AI winter; Hopfield's work revitalized large-scale interest in this field.

explainer.lead: John Hopfield is an American scientist (born 1933). His work spans biology, neuroscience, artificial neural network and applied psychology.
explainer.knownFor: He wrote: "The polarization field 'particles' analogous to photons will be called 'polaritons'." His polariton model is sometimes known as the Hopfield dielectric.

contributions.name: His doctoral dissertation was titled "A quantum-mechanical theory of the contribution of excitons to the complex dielectric constant of crystals".
This collaboration inspired the Computation and Neural Systems PhD program at Caltech in 1986, co-founded by Hopfield.
Hopfield was not included as a co-author in the papers but Anderson admitted the importance of Hopfield's contribution in various of his writings.
William C. Topp and Hopfield introduced the concept of norm-conserving pseudopotentials in 1973.

Together with David W. Tank, Hopfield developed a method in 1985–1986 for solving discrete optimization problems based on the continuous-time dynamics using a Hopfield network with continuous activation function.
